##### Complete Command And Option Coverage

The dispatch arms in `bin/ioc-runner`, its actual `--help` output, the argument
parser, and the shipped completion handler are separate comparison inputs.
Expected sets come from this reviewed table; a test must not derive its expected
set from the completion list it is checking. Compare exact sets, report missing
and extra entries, and retain raw output. Do not infer completeness from three
selected command names or from a count alone.

| Command | Target accepted by the runner | Completion contract | M10 treatment |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `generate` | IOC boot directory; current directory when omitted | Files and directories, as the existing handler supplies | Preserve path suggestions; do not redesign filtering |
| `install` | Configuration file or directory | Files and directories | Preserve path suggestions |
| `remove` | IOC name | Existing configuration names | Preserve |
| `start` | IOC name | Existing configuration names | Preserve |
| `stop` | IOC name | Existing configuration names | Preserve |
| `restart` | IOC name | Existing configuration names | Preserve |
| `status` | IOC name | Existing configuration names | Preserve |
| `enable` | IOC name | Existing configuration names | Preserve |
| `disable` | IOC name | Existing configuration names | Preserve |
| `view` | IOC name | Existing configuration names | Preserve |
| `log` | IOC name; effective file log in System/Local, rejected in Container | Existing configuration names in every selected mode, under the existing non-filtering completion policy | Add command, options and target routing; do not add Container file logging |
| `list` | No target required | `-v` and `-vv` after the command | Preserve; do not propose IOC names |
| `attach` | IOC name | Existing configuration names, or detach keys immediately after `--detach-key` | Preserve |
| `monitor` | IOC name | Existing configuration names | Preserve |
| `inspect` | IOC name | Existing configuration names | Preserve; actual privilege diagnostic is separate |

Every row is tested for command-name completion and its target class. The 12
IOC-target rows run under default System, `--local`, `--user`, and `--container`
forms. This is completion coverage; it does not claim every completed command
is valid in every mode or rerun unrelated service behavior.

| Option spellings | Value and actual meaning | Completion and verification boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--local`, `--user` | Local mode aliases | Preserve both and Local configuration selection |
| `--container` | Container mode | Preserve; use System configuration directory precedence |
| `-f`, `--force` | Force generate/install replacement; follow for `log` | Preserve both; do not invent `--follow` |
| `-n`, `--lines` | Separate positive integer; used by `log`; default is 40 when omitted | Add both; return no candidates while entering the number; afterwards resume command/option suggestions if no command exists, otherwise the existing command's target route |
| `-v`, `-vv` | List verbosity | Preserve both; other-command rejection stays in the runner |
| `--detach-key` | Separate control-key name for attach | Preserve `ctrl-a`, `ctrl-b`, `ctrl-]` suggestions and prefix filtering; these are a subset of accepted keys |
| `-V`, `--version` | Print version information and exit | Preserve both, including case distinction from `-v` |
| `-h`, `--help` | Print help and exit | Preserve both |

There are 14 option spellings. Global option suggestions remain broad: this
change does not build a second command-validity parser inside completion.
Do not introduce unsupported spellings such as `--lines=5`, `-n5`, `--follow`,
combined short options, or `--` as new CLI interfaces. No automatic numeric
suggestion is invented. An incomplete value is not a configuration name.

Configuration-directory checks cover each selected mode, mode flags before and
after the command, nonempty and empty environment overrides, and precedence:
`IOC_RUNNER_CONF_DIR` first; then `IOC_RUNNER_LOCAL_CONF_DIR` or
`IOC_RUNNER_SYSTEM_CONF_DIR`; then the existing HOME/System default. Use
separate real filesystem directories with distinguishable names. Include empty,
missing and unreadable directories under a real non-root caller, a non-conf
file, underscore/hyphen/numeric names, and a partial name. No service-state query
or config-content execution is part of completion. Invalid mixed-mode command
lines remain the runner's responsibility. Existing directory suggestions can
repeat because the handler uses both `compgen -f` and `compgen -d`; compare
membership rather than adding an unrelated deduplication change.

Setup's complete invocation surface is separate from runner completion:

| Entry point | Invocation forms | Plan boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Direct setup | no argument, `--full`, `--container`, `-h`, `--help` | Help becomes available to non-root; deployment still requires root |
| Direct setup ordering | `--full --help`, `--container -h`, `--full --container --help`, help before an unknown token, unknown token before help, conflicting modes without help, repeated mode flags | Preserve root parser ordering and help short-circuit behavior; specify unprivileged parser diagnostics separately from root deployment denial |
| Staging launcher | forwards direct-setup arguments after its own source/sudo checks | No promise of password-free launcher help; Q2 governs scan-directory environment forwarding |

Every help/error case records stdout, stderr, exit and a filesystem comparison.
The root gate remains before backend checks and all deployment work. After it
moves behind parsing, a non-root unknown option may report that parser error;
no non-root non-help case may reach a deployment operation.

For example, `ioc-runner -n 5 <TAB>` still needs a command, whereas
`ioc-runner log -n 5 <TAB>` and `ioc-runner -n 5 log <TAB>` complete an IOC
name. A value beginning with a dash must still remain a value position with
no suggestions; the runner owns its later rejection. Preserve existing
behavior after an IOC target is already present; adding target-count parsing
to completion is outside this change.

##### Implementation Plan

Implementation Authorization: 2026-10-15; auth20261015_073559, current owner direction to proceed

   mode-specific configuration-directory precedence, detach-key completion,
   and the existing global option-suggestion policy. Before command or target
   routing, handle a value immediately after `-n`/`--lines` by returning an
   empty candidate array; a completed number must not consume the IOC target.
   If no command has been supplied, retain command/option suggestions after

   and complete CLI, without a second implementation of either.
3. **Container identity diagnostics.** Change only the displayed mode in
   `validate_conf`'s individual mismatch branches. Extend the original
   `tests/test-container-lifecycle.bash` fixture: one incorrect user, one
   incorrect group, then the existing combined mismatch and valid control.
   Run these through whole CLI validation with native s6 and procServ present.
   Apply Q1 Keep and test non-root Container inspect at its actual common gate;
   preserve System's root requirement and Local's unprivileged path.
4. **Direct setup help.** Move the root gate after option parsing and before
   backend checks or deployment. Keep fixed PATH, umask and startup-variable
   hardening at entry. Preserve the current root parser's argument-order
   semantics, including help short-circuiting and invalid-option handling.
   Non-help deployment remains root-only. Add a real unprivileged caller
   matrix to the source-regression suite; never fake EUID or extract the parser.
5. **Logrotate failure message.** Replace the skip wording with an explicit
   setup-aborted/policy-not-deployed error, retaining exit 1 and cleanup.
   Confirm a genuine malformed-policy input, then run complete `--full`
   setup in disposable prepared VMs. Use native logrotate, systemctl and
   procServ; redirect filesystem destinations in a private mount namespace
   and retain protected-state snapshots. Check policy preservation, absence
   of subsequent CLI deployment, temporary-file cleanup, and a valid control.
   Full setup is not atomic: account/group state, shared directory metadata,
   the sudoers drop-in, log-directory ACLs, the unit template and a real
   daemon-reload precede logrotate validation. Capture and restore those
   earlier effects as well; preserving the old logrotate policy and CLI does
   not imply the whole guest was unchanged. The system manager is outside a
   filesystem mount namespace, so perform another native daemon-reload after
   the original unit paths are restored, and read back manager state.
   Do not reuse substituted executables from the type-isolation fixture as
   integration evidence; add a native setup-diagnostic helper if needed.
6. **Verify the retained direct setup interface.** Q2 is accepted Keep.
   Leave the launcher unchanged and verify the documented direct custom path
   in an isolated native s6 environment. Setup, the live supervisor and runner
   must use the same custom scan directory. No launcher-forwarding claim is made.
7. **Align evidence and documentation.** Update the changed suites' catalogs,
   matching `*_INVENTORY.md`, `tests/reporting-counts.csv`, and reporting
   inventories only where case identities or counts actually change.
   Update affected INSTALL/help/message passages and their M8 source bindings
   without promoting unrelated historical comparisons. Update INSTALL
   completion tables and its explicit omission paragraph, direct-setup help
   access, and the logrotate stop description. Check that the actual setup
   deploys the updated completion file and registers the handler in a fresh
   shell. Build the book and check links after those page edits.
8. **Review and finish.** Check Bash syntax and the ShellCheck warning gate,
   inspect the complete informational output, and run affected suites.
   Review root-gate ordering, privileged environment forwarding if selected,
   and failure cleanup separately. Obtain second-person review of help/docs
   and third-person review of real-path evidence under the established review
   procedure. Record exact results and restoration before M10 completion.

Execution environment: user-level completion/help checks first; one disposable
Debian Container with the repository's original lifecycle fixture for s6
diagnostics; Debian 13 and Rocky 8.10 prepared VMs for native full-setup failure
and restoration. Pin actual image/source identities at execution preflight.
Extra container OS runs are required only if a platform-specific result appears.
Read the VM preparation requirements in `tests/README.md` before requesting or
reusing guests. Drafting performs only unprivileged help/completion premise
checks; no privileged setup, package installation or VM/Container test is run.

Failure handling: capture expected nonzero exits without skipping cleanup;
stop task-owned services and namespaces, restore existing files and metadata,
and perform a fresh state readback. Retain failed evidence. If a real input
does not reach the intended branch, report the prerequisite as unmet rather
than replacing an internal function or tool result. A repeat of all M8
comparisons is outside this bounded change.

The complete error-handling suite must run as a dedicated non-root test account
in a disposable verification VM, with its own HOME, runtime directory and
native user manager. It must not use the workstation caller's manager or an
existing operator account. Source S37 performs a real Local install and can
call `systemctl --user enable --now epics-logrotate.timer` and daemon-reload;
redirecting configuration files alone does not isolate that manager. Before
the suite, verify the selected UID, HOME, runtime directory, bus address and
absence of pre-existing IOC/rotation units. Capture unit/timer states, then
stop and disable any task-created units and restore the account's original
files/state after the suite. Use a fresh login for the final readback. No
systemctl replacement is allowed. This environment requirement does not alter
the suite or make its existing mock-based cases native integration evidence;
T6-T11 retain their separate real-path requirements. Pure help/completion
premise checks may still run as the ordinary workstation user.

#### M11 - Report IOC startup exits and respect continued IOC shell errors

Origin: 1.4.2 / M11
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: [#166](https://github.com/jeonghanlee/epics-ioc-runner/issues/166)
Status: Complete

##### Summary

The committed runner reports a current child's nonzero normal exit code from complete,
PID-associated procServ records and returns runner exit 1 while the supervisor
remains active. A genuine continued iocsh quote error no longer causes a
text-only startup failure. The original generator revision below was built and
executed unchanged on Debian 13 and Rocky 8.10; actual break handling exits 2,
and continued cases retain readiness and a responding IOC. Signal termination,
normal exit 0, historical records and commanded restart teardown remain
distinct. Native default timing is 30 seconds for initialization and 3 seconds
for confirmation. Runtime restoration and fresh access checks are complete.
Both independent final implementation reviews accepted the corrected code,
documentation, handoff and bounded T1-T6 evidence. Commit
`ba787f0507d9ab157ed9241e3f71e904b9edc831` is on `origin/release-1.4.2`,
with all 15 prepared paths verified against the fetched commit. The issue body
records all six satisfied acceptance criteria and the verification limits;
#166 was closed as completed at 2026-10-16T01:44:55Z.

##### Scope

- `bin/ioc-runner`: system/local `start` and `restart` startup diagnostics,
  using actual procServ child status and the real IOC shell behavior.
- Real generated IOC fixtures: failure in st.cmd and in a loaded iocsh
  file, with per-file `on error break` and `on error continue` behavior.
- `docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md` and `docs/FAQ.md`: the resulting startup outcomes
  and distinction between active procServ and a terminated IOC child.
- `docs/adr/0001-restart-supervision-c1h.md`: an addendum for the changed
  startup outcome rule, preserving its historical decisions.
- Native regression coverage for the affected startup paths.

Out of scope: changing IOC generators or EPICS Base, systemd/procServ restart
policy, container diagnostics, local lingering, general pattern cleanup,
and completion of the whole-book M8 verification.

##### Completion Criteria

- A real continued IOC shell error with successful IOC startup does not
  become an IOC failure solely because an error message was printed.
- A failed startup that ends the IOC child with a nonzero normal exit
  reports that code plainly and returns failure, even if the unit is active.
- The check distinguishes normal exit codes from signal termination and
  does not classify commanded restart teardown or historical log content
  as a fresh startup failure.
- Per-file IOC shell behavior is verified with actual loaded scripts;
  generated-main exit mapping is identified before choosing the fixture.
- Existing real healthy, fatal, crash-loop and log-rotation regressions
  pass; the affected operator documentation matches observed behavior.

   neither an active procServ unit nor `128 + signal` is a normal child code.
   Match complete procServ status records to the supervised child PID and
   current attempt using the observed native record order. A bare number or
   IOC text containing the same words is insufficient. Retain association
   across confirmation scans; a status following its death banner may arrive
   in a later read. Wait only within the existing startup/confirmation bounds
   for that record before falling back, without inventing a numeric status.
4. Report current failed startup with the observed nonzero status and the
   existing log hint, returning runner exit 1. Proposed wording is
   `IOC '<name>' exited during startup (exit code <N>).` A code alone does
   not prove startup-script causation. Exclude historical attempts and
   commanded restart teardown; an earlier marker must not hide a later death.
   Preserve the existing failure fallback for unavailable/incomplete records.
   Narrow only continued-error cases demonstrated in step 2: readiness and
   a surviving IOC must not fail solely on that printed command error.
   A normal exit 0 alone is not readiness. Preserve the existing markerless
   active-unit timeout warning/exit 0 when there is no qualifying failure;
   do not print readiness success for it. Signal or repeated-death evidence
   keeps its existing failure meaning without a fabricated normal exit code.
   For `start` on an already running healthy IOC, retain the existing
   fast path; do not import old normal exits into this invocation. For an
   active `restart`, exclude the commanded old child's teardown by its
   identity, not by dropping the first normal-exit record regardless of PID.
   A new child's nonzero exit during this invocation is a failure even if a
   later automatic retry emits readiness. A pre-existing readiness marker

#### M12 - Explain local IOC lifetime and advise lingering on enable

Origin: 1.4.2 / M12
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: [#167](https://github.com/jeonghanlee/epics-ioc-runner/issues/167)
Status: Complete

##### Summary

Successful Local enable prints the existing non-fatal linger advice when the
native lookup does not report yes. The runner preserves enable failure,
lingering, IOC activity, and the existing install early returns. The Local
guide explains user-manager shutdown after logout under the host's effective
policy. Native Debian 13 and Rocky 8.10 verification and task restoration
passed on 2026-10-16. The remaining recovery-input exception path is corrected
under the additional authorization; 20 actual controller comparisons confirm
the changed behavior. Both reviewers accepted the correction without a
remaining in-scope finding. The accepted changes are committed and pushed as
`5e096e463bad74e31cea02296fab51499e15b434`. The issue body records all six
satisfied acceptance criteria, and #167 is closed as completed. Implementation,
bounded verification, restoration, repository landing and issue reconciliation
are complete.

##### Scope

- `docs/USER_GUIDE_LOCAL.md`, beside the boot/linger paragraph: explain
  that local IOCs run under the user manager and end when that manager
  stops after the last login session, under the target's effective policy.
- `bin/ioc-runner`: reuse the local install linger advice for local enable,
  preserving successful enable and non-fatal advice.
- Focused local-mode lifetime and advisory verification.

Out of scope: enabling linger automatically, changing login/session policy,
IOC startup diagnostics, system/container advisories, broad CLI cleanup,
and the unrelated M10 help/completion corrections.

##### Completion Criteria

- The guide covers logout lifetime and boot startup without promising
  immediate termination or ignoring UserStopDelaySec/target policy.
- Local enable with Linger=no succeeds and prints the same non-fatal
  advice as install; Linger=yes does not print the off advisory.
- Existing enable/disable behavior and installed IOC state are preserved;
  the runner does not change lingering.
- Real login/logout observations on isolated approved test identities
  confirm the published policy-specific lifetime statement.

- Decision Date: 2026-10-14. Record the correction proposal, implementation
  method and verification method, and prepare a separate issue draft. This
  authorizes planning; plan acceptance and implementation remain none.

as logout evidence. Record finite observations as bounded observations;
this test does not establish survival forever or test boot execution.

##### Scope

Prepare the configured socket parent in the rendered s6 run script before dropping privileges, preserve the existing identity, mode, and IOC PATH contract, stop before procServ on preparation failure, add a real container boot regression, and document startup and service regeneration requirements.

#### M14 - Separate fatal severity logs from IOC initialization failure

Origin: 1.4.2 / M14
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: [#165](https://github.com/jeonghanlee/epics-ioc-runner/issues/165)
Status: Complete

##### Summary

The case-insensitive fatal scan recognizes the `fatal` part of `sevr=fatal`.
At baseline `eb396aba52a0a2955cf1cd9c027e43e0788feeb8`, an earlier poll can
latch this as fatal and prevent later readiness from completing startup.
The M11 implementation waits for child status or the initialization deadline;
the original issue's immediate-failure description predates that change.
If the first poll sees the marker and error together, the marker branch runs
first and the pre-marker error can instead disappear from the final warning.
EPICS severity describes an error reported by a component; it does not itself
establish that the IOC process terminated or that all initialization failed.
The completed startup result must retain the module error without claiming
that all required IOC functions are healthy.

At the baseline, ADR 0004 explicitly preserves the pre-marker interpretation,
while FAQ severity descriptions promise corroboration only. M14 changes that
interpretation deliberately and aligns the affected documentation. The existing
text-emission reproduction establishes the scanner's behavior, not a real
module fault or its operational impact.

##### Scope

- `bin/ioc-runner`: the shared System/Local `start` and `restart` signal scan,
  retention of severity evidence across the readiness marker, and result text.
- Exact `sevr=fatal` marker handling after existing ANSI normalization;
  preserve a separate fatal diagnostic on the same line and the remaining
  fatal-pattern and death-banner rules.
- Existing native lifecycle fixtures and their reporting inventories, with
  an actual EPICS module error and complete shipped CLI execution.
- `tests/test-local-lifecycle.bash`, `tests/test-system-lifecycle.bash`,
  supporting original IOC fixtures, applicable lifecycle inventories,
  `tests/test-source-regression.bash`, its inventory and reporting counts.
- Task DB/protocol input for the original generated IOC, loaded through its
  public commands with unchanged main, generated DBD and module libraries.
- `docs/FAQ.md`, `docs/CLI_REFERENCE.md` and the affected decisions in
  `docs/adr/0004-severity-marker-corroboration.md` and ADR 0001.

Out of scope: repairing EPICS modules, changing IOC generators, changing
supervisor restart policy, Container diagnostics, general log-pattern cleanup,
new numeric child-exit reporting (M11), and M8 closure. No production fault
injection or shared-account policy change is part of this work.

##### Completion Criteria

- `sevr=fatal` alone before readiness does not force exit 1. Startup continues
  within the existing initialization timeout and preserves the error details.
- Readiness followed by the existing confirmation interval without observed
  child death returns 0 with a clear initialization-completed/error-log warning
  and log hint. It does not certify that all modules work.
- The pre-readiness error remains visible even after the scan advances past
  the marker; previous startups and commanded restart teardown are excluded.
- A separate fatal diagnostic, including one on the same line as the severity
  marker, and actual child-failure/crash-loop evidence retain failure behavior.
  Do not discard a whole line merely because it contains `sevr=fatal`.
- No readiness marker produces an explicit unconfirmed-initialization outcome;
  an unreadable log is reported as unreadable. Existing timeout return-code
  policy is preserved; absence of readiness is not reported as completed startup.
- Genuine module-error and independent child-failure cases pass through real
  IOC/procServ and the unchanged fixture path on both native OS families,
  System/Local, start/restart. Controlled text cases supplement this evidence.
- A behavior regression fails on the old runner and passes on the changed
  runner; no internal-function substitution counts as integration verification.
- Documentation and design decisions describe the same resulting behavior,
  and affected M8 source bindings and comparisons are refreshed afterwards.

##### Dependencies And Decisions

- Decision Date: 2026-10-14. Track this change as a separate M14 and issue,
  with M11 retaining IOC shell error policy and numeric child-exit reporting.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-14. Continue the remaining M8 comparisons before
  starting M14. Keep the M14 plan and issue open for later implementation;
  this ordering decision does not resolve either severity comparison.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-16. Resume M14 plan preparation after M10, M11 and
  M12 completion. Native execution and product changes have not started.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-16. Continue correction of the rejected native fault
  condition and one additional plan-review round. Runtime authority remains
  separate from this planning direction.
- Decision Date: 2026-10-16. Accept plan20261016_162050 and authorize
  P001-P006/V001-V005, retained-VM preparation, native verification and
  restoration. auth20261016_174408 records the execution direction.
- Observed 2026-10-16: the approved read-only preflight found missing native
  StreamDevice artifacts and no suitable retained SSH Local test operator on
  either guest. The accepted plan requires stopping on missing prerequisites.
  The owner subsequently selected preparation option 1 on 2026-10-16.
  The bounded module-build and temporary-account amendment is accepted and
  authorized under plan20261016_180600/auth20261016_180600. No new G dependency
  or scanner-contract change is introduced.
- No M/G prerequisite is asserted. M14 does not require M8 to be Complete;
  M8 must recheck affected claims after the product change.
- The requested behavior is to retain severity errors, wait for initialization,
  and distinguish completed startup with errors from observed IOC failure.
  This does not authorize treating an actual module error as harmless.

##### Implementation Plan

Plan Acceptance: 2026-10-16; plan20261016_180600
Implementation Authorization: 2026-10-16; auth20261016_180600, P001-P006/V001-V005 including the preparation amendment

###### Genuine Module Fault: StreamDevice Array Conversion

Use `tests/lib/test-startup-fixture.bash` and its original generator revision
`ee214deedc5594bb93cd0a77d42615b99783bbd0`. Keep the generated main, DBD and
compiled source unchanged. Test inputs are startup commands, task DB/protocol
files and trusted RELEASE assignments. The generator already supports `ASYN`
and `STREAM`, including `drvAsynIPPort.dbd` and `stream.dbd`; the installed
StreamDevice DBD must provide `devaaoStream`. No sequencer registrar is added.
Do not replace its main, mock iocsh, or print an expected error as the native
fault. The existing ServiceTestIOC revision remains
`91d42b2ceadec81a065d4cdf35936dbb8d77e202` for the other lifecycle cases.

The following caPutLog input was proposed and rejected during the first
second-person review on 2026-10-16. It is recorded as a rejected stimulus,
not as an executable T1 prescription:

```text
caPutLogInit("127.0.0.1:17011", 0, 0.1)
epicsThreadSleep(1)
iocInit
caPutLogShow(0)
```

In the inspected caPutLog source (`R4.1-18-gdafb0b2`), `caPutLog.c:106-108`
calls `caPutLogTaskStart` and returns on error. That function checks inactive
access security at `caPutLogTask.c:130-132`, emits `errlogMajor` and returns.
The later `caPutLogAsInit` fatal branch is therefore unreachable through this
input. `caPutLog not initialized` proves neither fatal severity nor a runner
regression. No module runtime was executed in reaching this source conclusion.

The replacement is a real output configuration error: an `aao` record uses
`FTVL=DOUBLE` with the string converter `%s`. Add these exact input files
under `tests/fixtures/` and copy them into the generated fixture's private boot
directory. They configure the actual module; they do not replace its code.

`startup-severity.db`:

```text
record(aao, "$(P)Conversion") {
    field(DESC, "Incompatible stream output format")
    field(DTYP, "stream")
    field(FTVL, "DOUBLE")
    field(NELM, "1")
    field(OUT, "@startup-severity.proto $(PROTOCOL) $(PORT) 0")
}
```

`startup-severity.proto`:

```text
bad_init {
    out "%s";
    @init { out "%s"; }
}
bad_process {
    out "%s";
}
```

After original support registration and before original initialization,
configure one IOC-private port and load the DB. Assign `M14_PORT_NUMBER` to an
unused loopback port, record it, and disable automatic connection. The failure
occurs while formatting, before any device write; no device emulator or real
device is required. Keep `STREAM_PROTOCOL_PATH` pointed at the copied input's
absolute directory and load the DB by absolute path. The execution record
provides the exact expanded path and a unique `M14_PREFIX` ending in `:`.

```text
epicsEnvSet("STREAM_PROTOCOL_PATH", "$(M14_INPUT_DIR)")
drvAsynIPPortConfigure("M14_CONVERSION", "127.0.0.1:$(M14_PORT_NUMBER)", 0, 1, 0)
dbLoadRecords("$(M14_INPUT_DIR)/startup-severity.db", "P=$(M14_PREFIX),PORT=M14_CONVERSION,PROTOCOL=bad_init")
```

Source chain, inspected at StreamDevice revision
`668d1d525509604ab4ccd7382022dfb469c99841` and Base revision
`bf11a0c31c919ba85ba2e23b72bcf0b5f9f62e77`:

1. Base `aaoRecord.c:init_record` sets `NORD=1` for `NELM=1` before calling
   device initialization. StreamDevice `devaaoStream.c:initRecord` allocates
   the real array and calls `streamInitRecord` with the actual read/write
   callbacks. `Stream::initRecord` attaches to the configured asyn interface,
   parses the protocol and starts its `@init` handler.
2. `StreamCore::evalOut` calls `formatOutput` before `busLockRequest`.
   `formatOutput` calls `Stream::formatValue`, which dispatches to the actual
   `writeData` callback for an unredirected `%s`. With one DOUBLE element,
   its string-conversion default emits `errlogSevPrintf(errlogFatal, ...)`
   and returns ERROR. The expected diagnostic contains
   `writeData <record>: can't convert from DBF_DOUBLE to string`.
3. The protocol finishes synchronously with FormatError;
   `Stream::protocolFinishHook` records internal CALC_ALARM status and signals
   init completion. The false return also propagates through `startProtocol`,
   so `Stream::initRecord` reports `Can't start @init handler` and returns
   before `initDone.wait()`. This internal status is not an observed record
   STAT value. Base's `doInitRecord0` invokes record support without propagating
   that record's return as the whole `iocBuild` result. Actual record fields,
   readiness and continued IOC operation must still be observed at runtime.
4. Asyn `drvAsynIPPortConfigure` registers its normal interfaces with
   automatic connection disabled. StreamDevice `connectToBus` binds its
   asynUser and interfaces and returns true even when disconnected. Missing
   port registration, parsing failure or an earlier unsupported DBD is a
   failed prerequisite, not the selected conversion fault.

Use three input variants. For the separated pre-marker case, replace only
the original `iocInit` command with `iocBuild`, `epicsThreadSleep(1)` and
`iocRun`; Base's own `iocInit` calls `iocBuild() || iocRun()`. Keep the original
`on error break`. For the ordinary pre-marker case, keep `iocInit` unchanged
with `bad_init` and no added pause. This does not guarantee one scanner poll;
deterministic same-poll coverage belongs to the whole-runner outer-log tests.
For the post-marker case, select `bad_process` at DB load, keep `iocInit`,
then run the following commands before the confirmation interval ends:

```text
on error continue
dbpf("$(M14_PREFIX)Conversion.PROC", "1")
on error break
dbpr("$(M14_PREFIX)Conversion", 2)
```

The narrow continue block permits the genuine record-processing error to be
reported without changing the intended surviving-IOC case into an M11 shell
exit case. Record its actual return and log, and keep the separate M11 break
controls. Require the conversion diagnostic and observed timing; neither a
sleep nor a source prediction proves the scanner saw a particular window.

For every variant, record actual fatal output, record `STAT`, `SEVR`, `NORD`
and `PACT` through real `dbpr`/console, failed conversion, IOC readiness,
console response and native child records separately. Do not equate an
initialized IOC or a record alarm with a working output function. After plan
acceptance, first confirm the installed ASYN/STREAM revisions, library hashes,
DBD registration and source equivalence to this call chain on both guests.
Run the unchanged baseline against the same genuine inputs before product
edits. Missing fatal output or a different path stops T1; no printed substitute,
private-function call, generator alteration or resource-exhaustion fault may
replace it. The sequencer argument candidate remains unused because this
generator links the library without registering the public `seq` command.

###### Scanner And Result Contract

1. Normalize ANSI SGR and apply the existing benign-history filter first.
   In the fatal-only view, mask only lowercase `sevr=fatal` with non-identifier
   boundaries on both sides. Keep surrounding text and scan it for the
   existing fatal patterns. Repeated markers must all be handled; a separate
   `FATAL`, `Segmentation fault`, `undefined symbol` or `error while loading`
   on the same line still counts. Case variants and identifier fragments
   must not gain a new exemption. The corroboration view retains the original
   severity text; extra patterns remain corroboration only.
2. Inspect the portion before the raw readiness marker for pre-marker fatal
   evidence, including when both first arrive in one poll. Post-marker fatal
   text alone keeps the existing warning policy. Native nonzero child status
   retains priority over the marker and any later automatic retry.
3. Retain invocation-local severity evidence before the phase transition and
   during confirmation. Keep the first three distinct normalized severity
   lines, consistent with the existing display limit, and a separate observed
   flag. Do not retain whole repeated windows or create a new public setting.
   Observed lines survive rotation and truncation; bytes never observed before
   deletion cannot be recovered or claimed. Keep raw offsets, inode/tail-hash
   checks, complete-record parsing, child PID association and commanded old
   child exclusion. Keep the active-start no-op path unchanged.
4. Readiness plus confirmation without failure returns 0. If retained severity
   is present, report that initialization completed with error logs, show the
   retained details and log hint, and ask the operator to check affected
   functions. Do not print unqualified successful startup for that case.
   Other post-marker corroboration retains its current heuristic warning.
5. No readiness keeps the existing active-unit timeout return 0 with an
   unconfirmed-initialization warning, or an unreadable-log warning when that
   is the observed condition. A severity observation remains visible there;
   no completed-startup wording is allowed. Actual nonzero child exit,
   independent pre-marker fatal evidence and crash-loop failures remain exit 1.
   Keep defaults of 30 seconds initialization, 3 seconds confirmation and
   0.2 seconds polling. Do not change supervisor policy or infer module health.

###### Required Behavior Matrix

| Case group | Stimulus and observation | Required outcome |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Native module error | StreamDevice DOUBLE-to-string conversion failure, before readiness with a pause, ordinary initialization without an added pause, and after readiness; observe failed record function and console separately | Qualified completed startup, exit 0 with retained severity; Pending until the native prerequisite and full comparison run |
| Verb/state coverage | Each module-error variant under stopped start, active restart and stopped restart; already-active start as a separate no-op control | Both OS families and modes; old teardown excluded; no historical warning invented by the no-op |
| Independent failure | Real original IOC break/nonzero exit, signal and zero-before-init controls; native death after severity and readiness | Existing numeric or fallback failure behavior; no signal-to-normal-code invention |
| Exact matching | Whole runner over controlled outer log input: lowercase bounded marker, ANSI marker, repeated markers, case variants, identifier fragments, marker plus a separate fatal diagnostic on one line | Only exact severity exemption; other fatal evidence preserved; document native versus controlled evidence |
| Poll ordering | Error first, marker first, same window, and error at the final confirmation scan | Pre-marker severity retained; post-marker-only fatal remains corroboration; native nonzero exit takes priority |
| Log boundaries | Historical error before invocation, active restart teardown, observed error followed by inode replacement/copytruncate/regrowth, and incomplete log records | No old-run false warning; observed error survives reset; no promise to recover unseen deleted bytes |
| Missing evidence | No readiness while active, unreadable log, and readiness followed by genuine termination | Explicit unconfirmed/unreadable/failure outcomes; never unqualified completion |

The genuine T1 matrix is two OS families x two modes x three starting
states/verbs for each error placement. Controlled log cases exercise the whole
runner and are supplementary filesystem-boundary tests, not module-fault
evidence. Freeze final case IDs and expected outcomes before launch and derive
counts from the actual catalog; do not invent PASS totals from this plan.
Review the final implementation and evidence through the existing third-person
and second-person lanes, with one bounded correction cycle. Leave T1-T5
Pending until their real paths execute. Refresh affected source captures and
M8 C00700/C00722 only from resulting evidence; M8 closure, St04 and G2 remain
outside this milestone.

#### G1 - Test fixture account `opc` in `ioc` with linger

Origin: 1.4.2 / G1
Identity History: none
GitHub Issue: none
Status: Complete

##### Summary

M9's L4 scenario needs one account that is both an `ioc` group member and a
local-mode user with systemd linger. The fixture accounts come from the
`testusers` role of ansible-provision (`roles/testusers/`), baked into the
iocrunner golden: `opa` and `opb` are operators without linger, and `usera`
and `userb` have linger but are outside `ioc`.

##### Completion Condition

- The `testusers` role creates `opc` in the `ioc` group with linger enabled.
- Both reused test consumers carry `opc`.

The bake that carries `opc` was a third condition until 2026-09-28, when the
owner moved it to G2.

##### Verification Results

Checked on both test consumers with `id -nG opc`, which must list `ioc`,
and the presence of `/var/lib/systemd/linger/opc`, the same form as the
fixture check in `gate/RUNBOOK.md`.

Observed on 2026-09-28 (UTC):

- The first condition is met by ansible-provision `32ea95f` on
  `origin/m14-middleware-reconcile` (jeonghanlee/ansible-provision#27),
  which adds `test_users_operators_linger: [opc]` and the task that creates
  each such account in `ioc` with linger; the other fixture accounts are
  unchanged.
- The second condition is met: `make op.testusers.<vacuum>` from that
  ansible-provision checkout, with host inventories generated by
  cloud-provision's `bin/generate_ansible_inventory.bash`, returned rc 0 and
  `failed=0` on both test consumers; on both, `id -nG opc` printed
  `opc ioc`, `/var/lib/systemd/linger/opc` existed, and `opa` and `opb`
  still had no linger file.
- The bake condition, then open, moved to G2 the same day.
